Title: Diagnosis of failing test `testUnionOfVariableAndNode`
Details:
1. The test creates an XML Document with a root element `<MAIN>` containing two `<A/>` child elements.
2. It then creates a JXPathContext from the XML Document.
3. A variable named "var" with value "varValue" is declared in the context.
4. The test iterates over pointers obtained by the XPath expression `"$var | /MAIN/A"`, which is a union of the variable reference `$var` and the node-set `/MAIN/A`.
5. The failure likely occurs due to how the `iteratePointers` method processes a union XPath expression involving both a variable and nodes.
6. The union XPath expression combines different types: one is a single variable (probably resolved to a value), and others are XML nodes.
7. There may be an issue in the implementation of `JXPathContext.iteratePointers(String)` or the underlying XPath compiler/executor that fails or produces unexpected results when union of variables and nodes is used.
8. The test does not assert the `sz`, but implicitly expects iteration to succeed without exceptions for this mixed union expression.

In summary, the bug arises from handling unions in XPath involving variables and nodes inside `iteratePointers`.

The most relevant method to inspect and fix is `JXPathContext.iteratePointers(String)` where such XPath expressions are parsed and executed. Also code dealing with variable resolution and union evaluation in the XPath implementation may be the root cause.

Suggested method to fix:
- org.apache.commons.jxpath.JXPathContext.iteratePointers(java.lang.String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
